summary: Make workspace trust an explicit, provisioned setting for every non-interactive checkout instead of relying on a dialog that never appears: set `[projects."<abs-path>"] trust_level = "trusted"` in ~/.codex/config.toml for Codex, and `projects["<repo-root>"].hasTrustDialogAccepted = true` in ~/.claude.json for Claude Code, provisioning both in CI images, ephemeral cloud sessions and fresh worktrees; for repositories you do not own, do the opposite deliberately (`--setting-sources user`, `--bare`, `disabledMcpjsonServers`) so the reduced configuration is a chosen state rather than an accident.

evidence.summary: 'What runs before you trust a folder' documents that the trust dialog never appears in `claude -p` or SDK sessions, lists what is withheld (permissions.allow, additionalDirectories, subagent frontmatter hooks and inline mcpServers, @skills-dir plugins, extraKnownMarketplaces, .mcp.json headersHelper), and names the manual key projects["<path>"].hasTrustDialogAccepted in ~/.claude.json plus the hardening flags for untrusted repos.
projects.<path>.trust_level marks a project or worktree trusted or untrusted; untrusted projects skip project-scoped .codex/ layers including project-local config, hooks and rules.
2026-08-20 Codex changelog: untrusted projects no longer supply project-level AGENTS.md instructions.
Open feature request for a trustedDirectories setting to auto-trust directories at startup, confirming that provisioning trust today means writing the config key by hand.

conditions: CI runners, ephemeral cloud sessions, containers, or freshly cloned worktrees where an interactive trust dialog cannot be answered
Repositories the operator owns and whose committed configuration is reviewed
Surfaces: Claude Code (v2.1.238+ behavior for headersHelper and inline mcpServers) and OpenAI Codex (2026-08-20 onward)
not_applicable_when: Repositories from untrusted third parties — trusting them grants repository-controlled hooks, MCP servers and helper commands execution on your machine
Interactive local sessions where the dialog is answered once and persists
Organizations that deliberately run agents in reduced-configuration mode as a security posture

expected_effect.primary: The same repository and prompt produce the same loaded configuration in every environment, so convention violations stop being misdiagnosed as ignored instructions and instruction files stop being rewritten to fix a loading problem.

risks: Pre-trusting is a real security-boundary decision: repository-supplied hooks, MCP servers, env blocks and helper commands then run without prompting
Blanket-trusting a parent directory does not satisfy the per-folder rows and gives false confidence
Trust semantics changed at v2.1.207/2.1.238/2.1.246 and on Codex at 2026-08-20; a provisioned key may need updating
Writing ~/.claude.json or ~/.codex/config.toml from automation can conflict with the CLI's own writes
revalidate_when: Claude Code ships a first-class trustedDirectories setting (issue #12737)
Either surface changes which artifacts trust gates
A new agent product adopts a trust flag over project instruction files
